chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about breaking the fast of the expiation for an oath, and the expiation for Dhihar, and the expiation for killing. He said: If fasting two consecutive months is upon a man, and he breaks his fast or falls ill during the first month, then upon him is that he repeats the fasting. And if he fasted the first month, and fasted part of the second month, then an excuse presents itself to him for which there is a valid reason, then upon him is that he makes up for it.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one breaks the fast of two consecutive months required for expiation due to illness?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic distinction between a complete reset of the obligation and a simple makeup (qada) based on the timing of the interruption during the two-month period. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity (ittisal) required for specific expiations, ensuring that the spiritual rigor of the fast is preserved unless a valid excuse (‘udhr) intervenes. The ruling underscores the balance between divine ease and the seriousness of fulfilling vows or penalties in Islamic law.
